title: Leviathan: A Unified System for General-Purpose Near-Data Computing
problem: Data movement costs are becoming a critical bottleneck in computing systems. Existing near-data computing architectures have limited applicability and difficult programming models.
motivation: Near-data computing can significantly reduce data movement costs and improve both performance and energy efficiency in future computing systems.
method: Leviathan creates a unified system for near-data computing—performing calculations where data is stored instead of moving data to a processor. It uses reactive programming (responding automatically to data events) to determine what to compute, where in the memory system to compute it (caches, memory levels), and when to execute—decisions that normally require manual optimization by programmers. By combining multiple near-data computing approaches into one integrated platform with cache-integrated execution, the system adapts to different computational strategies without needing separate custom designs.
key_novelty: Leviathan provides a single unified system with reactive programming that automatically adapts to multiple near-data computing strategies, eliminating the need for separate custom architectures for each approach.
contributions: Taxonomy of NDC designs identifying what, where, and when to compute as key dimensions
Unified architecture and reactive-programming interface for near-cache NDC
Integration of multiple NDC paradigms in a single general-purpose system
Demonstrates 1.5×-3.7× speedup and 22%-77% energy reduction with only ~6% area overhead
limitations: Limitations and challenges of the approach are not discussed in the abstract.
